_comment: Hand-authored. The corridor data loader and the flag helpers, bank 7 $EF6C-$EFF2 (the bit-mask table $EFD8 is claimed elsewhere). The generator for 20-traced.json subtracts these.

regions.name: CORRIDOR DATA LOADER: the corridor's scenes
regions.description: Called by JSR from $EC9C, after the launch flight ($F282). $EECC (the common start: $56 := $FF, attribute patterns, read the record at $E4, common scene 0), then bank 5 $8000 with A = 1 (scene 1, the corridors' common scene), then the corridor's own scene $EF55[$51] (23 entries: $20 $21 $21 $22 $22 $23 $23 $24 $24 $26 $26 $21 $21 $22 $22 $23 $23 $24 $24 $25 $25 $25 $20), a wait for the decompressor ($D7C3), and bank 5 $8036 (-> $A430, not read through). RUN (corridor 5, after the flight): $5C = $23 = $EF55[5]; $EF6C at frame 373 of the start, $E560 nine frames later, finished at 390.

regions.name: Corridor start: remember the score
regions.description: Copies the six score bytes $0170-$0175 to $04B9-$04BE (Y = 6 down to 1). The corridor's boss routine turns the difference into the points gained, which the TGL reward uses. RUN with a score of 1..6: $04B9-$04BE = 1..6, $04B8 and $04BF untouched.

regions.name: Corridor start: remember the maximum life
regions.description: $78 := $47. A TGL CONTINUE restores $47 from $78 (see the start-mode notes). RUN.

regions.name: Corridor start: set the corridor flags
regions.description: $30 := ($30 AND $9F) OR $50: bits 6 and 4 set (a corridor; the NMI moves the split marker), bit 5 cleared (not a special screen), bit 7 and the low bits kept. RUN: $A7 -> $D7; after a real start $50.

regions.name: Corridor start: the screen-data block
regions.description: Selects bank 4 and calls its entry $8000 with A = $51, which returns the corridor's block address in $18/$19 (the entry returns a pointer rather than running code).

regions.name: Corridor start: start the stage engine and fill the screen
regions.description: $E560 (reset the row engine, read the block's first trigger) and $E5BD (prime a whole screen of 15 rows at 16 px a frame); see the stage-engine notes. RUN: $E560 at frame 382, the priming finished at 390.

regions.name: Corridor start: back to bank 5
regions.description: JMP $D755: bank 5 is selected and the routine returns to the corridor loader.

regions.name: Is flag (A - 1) set? - the corridor-cleared test
regions.description: In: A = the corridor number c (1-21). Tests bit (c - 1) of the array $04A9-$04AB (corridors 1-8 in $04A9, 9-16 in $04AA, 17-21 in $04AB) through the bit-address helper $EFC7. Out: carry CLEAR = the bit is set (the corridor is cleared), carry SET = not. $EFB5 is shared with the item-flag test below. RUN: after marking 1, 5, 8, 9, 10, 17 and 21 exactly those gave carry clear; the bytes were $91 $03 $11.

regions.name: Mark corridor A cleared
regions.description: Sets bit (A - 1) of $04A9-$04AB. Called from the stage end ($ECE4) for corridors 1-20; the flags are part of the password payload (bytes 0-16 land at $04A0-$04B0). RUN.

regions.name: Bit address: byte index and mask for a bit number
regions.description: Slot $C078. In: A = a bit number n. Out: Y = n / 8, A and $10 = 1 << (n AND 7) (the mask from the 8-byte table at $EFD8). Used by the cleared flags, the item flags and the corridor seals ($04B1/$04B2). RUN: n = 0, 1, 7, 8, 15, 16, 20, 39 gave (Y, mask) = (0,1) (0,2) (0,$80) (1,1) (1,$80) (2,1) (2,$10) (4,$80).

regions.name: Is item flag A set?
regions.description: Tests bit A of the array at $04A0 (the pick-up and shop flags: a room's sub-id is its flag number). Out: carry CLEAR = set, SET = not, through the shared tail $EFB5. Used by the special-screen loader for the shops and by the item rooms. RUN: flags 0, 9 and 20 set were the only carry-clear results among 0-21.

regions.name: Set item flag A
regions.description: Sets bit A of the array at $04A0. RUN: flags 0, 9, 20 -> $04A0 = $01, $04A1 = $02, $04A2 = $10.
